# Collective Quantum Programming

> Sample complexity of programming a parallel batch of unknown support reflections from flat-rank quantum states.

## Scientific entry points

- [Overview](README.md): Task, theorem, explicit comparison, limits and reproduction.
- [Science index](science/README.md): Connected reading order and proof dependencies.
- [Model](science/model.md): Independent programs P/r, known rank, deterministic unconditional processing, hard specimen budget and joint unhalved diamond error.
- [Collision bound](science/collision_bound.md): Nonasymptotic variance-sensitive reduced-channel lemma.
- [Collective construction](science/parallel_program.md): Swap moments, exact variance, repeated collisions and batching.
- [Converse](science/converse.md): Nearby-support fidelity and phase-amplification lower bound.
- [Resources](science/resources.md): Pair gates, symmetric sweeps, finite rotation synthesis, memory and preparation charges.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): Large-batch optimality, explicit DME comparison and unresolved small-batch dependence.

## Evidence and attribution

- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md): Model-level comparisons and inherited methods.
- [Bibliography](references/references.bib): Version-specific primary references.
- [Verification](verification/README.md): Commands, actual outputs and numerical limitations.
- [Verification code](verification/verify.py): Small-dimensional matrix checks.
- [Recorded results](verification/results.json): Actual output of the documented run.

## Claim boundaries

The matching law N*=Theta(r k^2/epsilon) holds for k>=r, 1<=r<d and 0<epsilon<=1/8. The construction has order (r^2 k+r k^2)/epsilon for all positive k. The exact-angle theorem and the finite-gate resource allocation have different constants. No matching small-batch theorem, controlled unknown reflection, online adaptive oracle, catalyst return, generic classical-compiler separation or runtime advantage is claimed. Public analytical proofs are authoritative; numerical checks do not establish the universal theorem or priority.
